claims.text: An enhanced free-energy sampling method can integrate DFT-derived magnetic parameters with Monte Carlo or other enhanced-sampling techniques.
DFT-derived magnetic parameters can incorporate spin-fluctuation effects relevant to non-equiatomic HEAs.
The proposed computational method can be used to tune the magnetic transition temperature of non-equiatomic HEAs.
The proposed computational method can be used to tune the magnetocaloric response of non-equiatomic HEAs.
The target non-equiatomic HEAs possess significant chemical disorder.
The proposed sampling scheme can capture the interplay between spin fluctuations and configurational disorder.
The proposed sampling scheme can account for finite-size effects in thin-film or nanostructured HEAs.
Chemical disorder and configurational complexity mediate spin interactions in the HEA microstructure.
The relevant free-energy landscape contains contributions from spin fluctuations and chemical disorder.
Explicitly resolving this free-energy landscape enables systematic tuning of magnetic transition temperatures.
Explicitly resolving this free-energy landscape enables systematic tuning of magnetocaloric entropy changes.
Computational free-energy guidance can inform alloy-composition design.
Computational free-energy guidance can inform nanostructural design.
Implementing designs selected by the method will shift the magnetic transition temperature.
Implementing designs selected by the method will optimize the magnetocaloric entropy change.
Method-informed HEAs will provide enhanced cooling performance relative to baseline non-equiatomic HEAs.
Uncertainty in modeling finite-size effects may limit the method's tuning efficacy.
Uncertainty in quantifying spin-fluctuation contributions may limit the method's tuning efficacy.
Experimental data on low-dimensional magnetocaloric HEAs are limited.
